props.title: Just One of the Guys

sections.content: **Just One of the Guys** (1985) brilliantly subverts gender-swap comedies through its sharp take on workplace sexism and high school politics. Following aspiring journalist Terry Griffith who disguises herself as a male student to prove gender bias, it builds on Shakespeare's gender-bending template seen in **Twelfth Night** adaptations like **She's the Man** (2006). The film stands out from other 80s teen comedies like **Fast Times at Ridgemont High** (1982) by tackling serious themes of discrimination while maintaining its comedic edge.

sections.content: The gender-swap comedy genre peaked in the 1980s, with films like **Tootsie** (1982) and **Victor/Victoria** (1982) examining gender roles through comedy. What sets **Just One of the Guys** apart is its youth perspective and journalism angle, predating similar themes in **Never Been Kissed** (1999). Joyce Hyser's committed performance as Terry navigating both gender identities grounds the film's more outlandish moments in authentic emotion.

The film's influence can be seen in later teen comedies tackling gender politics, from **She's the Man** (2006) to **Easy A** (2010). Its blend of commentary and comedy created a template for addressing serious social issues through accessible teen narratives. The romantic subplot between Terry and Rick adds complexity to the gender exploration, forcing both characters to confront their assumptions. SUBHEAD: Gender Identity in 1980s Teen Cinema

sections.content: While other 80s teen films like **Sixteen Candles** (1984) and **The Breakfast Club** (1985) explored class and social hierarchies, **Just One of the Guys** uniquely focused on gender discrimination in both academic and professional settings. The film's commentary on journalism's male-dominated culture remains relevant, connecting to later works like **Morning Glory** (2010) and **Late Night** (2019).
